head: 13,000 people, one land lottery
fact: In 1901, about 13,000 people camped in tents near the future Hobart for the land lottery on the former Kiowa-Comanche-Apache Reservation.
ask: Does your family have a Hobart origin story? Tell us in the comments.

head: A town in five days
fact: The Hobart townsite was open prairie on August 1, 1901. The lot sale began August 6, and the new town had 2,530 residents.
ask: What would you have built first? Tell us in the comments.

head: Who is Hobart named for?
fact: Hobart is named for Garret A. Hobart, Vice President of the United States from 1897 to 1899.
ask: Did you know that? Drop a comment if this was new to you.

head: Ragtown
fact: In its earliest days, Hobart was nicknamed "Ragtown."
ask: Any other Hobart nicknames you remember? Tell us in the comments.

head: Hobart by 1903
fact: Just two years after the land opening, Hobart had electric lights, an ice plant, a flour mill and four national banks.

head: Hobart at statehood
fact: When Oklahoma became a state in 1907, Hobart had 3,136 residents.

head: Hobart's biggest year
fact: Hobart's population peaked at 5,380 in the 1950 census.

head: A railroad landmark
fact: The Rock Island Depot in Hobart is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
ask: Have you ever been inside? Tell us your memory in the comments.

head: Historic Hobart
fact: Downtown Hobart, the Kiowa County Courthouse, Hobart City Hall and the Hobart Public Library are all on the National Register of Historic Places.

head: The Frisco line
fact: The Frisco Railway runs north and south along the eastern edge of Hobart.
